nodes.summary: For $a, b, a', b' \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, So the product of two Pauli operators is a Pauli operator up to a sign, as in Preskill's description of the Pauli group $G_n$ (Section 7.9.1). Taking $a' = a$, $b' = b$ gives $(X^a Z^b)^{*} X^a Z^b = I$: each $X^a Z^b$ is unitary (property (i) there).
nodes.title: Product of two Pauli operators

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be the projector onto a code on $n$ qubits. The code has distance at least $d$ if every Pauli operator $X^a Z^b$ of weight less than $d$ satisfies for some scalar $c_{a,b}$. In an orthonormal basis $|\bar\imath\rangle$ of the code this is $\langle \bar\imath | X^a Z^b | \bar\jmath \rangle = c_{a,b} \delta_{ij}$. nodes.title: Distance of a quantum code (lower bound)

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be an orthogonal projector onto a code on $n$ qubits with distance at least $d$. Then the set of Pauli errors $X^a Z^b$ of weight $t$ with $2t + 1 \le d$ is correctable on the code, by a single recovery channel. This is Preskill's statement in Section 7.3.1: "a QECC with distance $d = 2t + 1$ can correct $t$ errors".
nodes.title: A code of distance `2t + 1` corrects `t` errors

nodes.summary: The Pauli operator $X^{a + a'} Z^{b + b'}$, which is the product of $X^a Z^b$ and $X^{a'} Z^{b'}$ up to a sign, has weight at most the sum of their weights: It acts trivially on every qubit where both factors act trivially, so its support is contained in the union of their supports. This is the step "$E_a^{\dagger} E_b$ has weight at most $2t$" in Preskill's argument that a distance-$(2t + 1)$ code corrects $t$…
nodes.title: Weight of a product of Pauli operators

nodes.summary: The weight of the Pauli operator $X^a Z^b$ equals the Hamming norm of the vector $i \mapsto (a_i, b_i)$ in $(\mathbb{F}_2 \times \mathbb{F}_2)^n$, that is the number of indices with $(a_i, b_i) \ne (0, 0)$. The vector $(a, b) \in \mathbb{F}_2^{2n}$ is the symplectic representation of the Pauli operator up to phase used in Preskill's Section 7.9.2, so the quantum weight is the classical Hamming weight over the…
nodes.title: Pauli weight as a Hamming norm

nodes.summary: The weight of the Pauli operator $X^a Z^b$ on $n$ qubits ($a, b \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$) is the number of qubits on which it acts by a nontrivial Pauli matrix $X$, $Z$ or $XZ$. Preskill defines it for the strings in $\{I, X, Y, Z\}^{\otimes n}$: "the weight is the number of qubits acted on by a nontrivial Pauli matrix". The same count appears in the statement that CSS codes correct $\lfloor (d-1)/2 \rfloor$ errors.
nodes.title: Weight of a Pauli operator

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be the orthogonal projector onto a code of dimension $2^k$, with $k \ge 1$, in the space of $n$ qubits, and suppose the code has distance at least $d$. Then stated as $k + 2(d - 1) \le n$ to avoid truncated subtraction. This is Preskill's equation (7.103). It resembles the classical Singleton bound $n - k \ge d - 1$, with twice the redundancy, and the $[[5, 1, 3]]$ code attains it.
nodes.title: The quantum Singleton bound
